presets.label: Provider
presets.hint: Fills the server, port and security; the choice itself is not saved.

names.google: Google Workspace / Gmail (with an app password)
names.google-relay: Google SMTP relay (no password, by IP address)

help.google: Google does not accept the account password for SMTP. The user name is the full e-mail address; the password is that account's 16-character app password (the account needs 2-Step Verification; an organisation's administrator may have turned the option off). If app passwords cannot be used, choose “Google SMTP relay”.
help.google-relay: No password: Google recognises the e-mail by the public IP address this server reaches the internet from. In the Google Admin console, under Apps → Google Workspace → Gmail → Routing → SMTP relay service, add a rule that accepts mail only from the specified IP addresses, and list that public IP address. The sender address must be in your own domain; the user name stays empty.
help.microsoft365: The user name is the mailbox's full address and the password is that account's password. The Microsoft 365 administrator must turn on authenticated SMTP (SMTP AUTH) for this mailbox; with the tenant's Security defaults on, sign-in with a password does not work. The sender address must be the mailbox's address.
help.hosting: Enter the SMTP server name, the user name (usually the full e-mail address) and the password your hosting company gave you. If they say 465 and SSL/TLS, choose those.
help.company: Type the name of the company's mail server or relay. If it accepts this machine by its IP address, the user name stays empty. If a user name is needed, choose STARTTLS: over a plain connection a user name may only go to this server itself.
